harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed an Ansible playbook on node1 (connection: local) that keeps AppArmor (Ubuntu's mandatory access control framework) enforcing and installs/starts a Python-based inventory application as a systemd service (inventory-app) bound to 0.0.0.0:8181, serving JSON inventory data at /inventory. Verified reachability over the network from node2. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol on both managed nodes, one at a time, each verified via boot_id change and post-restart health checks.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Ubuntu 24.04 (AppArmor is the MAC framework here, not SELinux); confirmed AppArmor active/enforcing (24 profiles enforce); found no existing inventory app and no firewall (ufw inactive)
Found node2 pre-provisioned with Ansible core 2.20.5, but node1 had no ssh server, so installed Ansible on node1 and ran the playbook locally there (connection: local) instead of via SSH from node2

Wrote and deployed an Ansible playbook (/root/ansible-inventory-app/site.yml on node1) that: ensures the apparmor package/service is present, started, and enabled; verifies enforcing mode via aa-status --enforced both before and after deployment; deploys inventory.json and a Python HTTP server (app.py) under /opt/inventory-app; installs and enables a systemd unit inventory-app.service listening on 0.0.0.0:8181; waits for the port to come up
Ran the playbook successfully (ok=12 changed=5 failed=0)
Verified the inventory app locally on node1 and remotely from node2 via curl to the node IP on port 8181, confirming JSON inventory data returned and AppArmor stayed enforcing throughout
Captured pre-restart boot_id baselines for node1 and node2, plus healthy-service evidence (apparmor enforcing, inventory-app active/enabled, curl success)

Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded so the acknowledgement returned before disconnect), polled until reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified AppArmor enforcing plus inventory-app active/enabled plus successful curl post-restart

Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot the same way, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified Ansible still functional plus cross-node curl to node1's inventory app still succeeding

evidence.requirement: Inventory application served on TCP port 8181 on node1
evidence.summary: Playbook run completed with changed=5/failed=0; curl to $NODE_IP:8181/inventory on node1 and from node2 both returned the JSON inventory payload

evidence.requirement: Mandatory access control (AppArmor) remains enforcing while the app is served
evidence.summary: aa-status showed apparmor active with 24 profiles enforcing before deployment; playbook's post-deploy aa-status --enforced check passed; confirmed again via aa-status after the app was live
Ansible installed on node1; playbook site.yml written and transferred; ansible-playbook run produced the full task recap with no failures
Captured boot_id f9bf293d... and confirmed apparmor enforcing / inventory-app active / curl success prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent poll returned connection reset (node down) then success with new boot_id 7e7304b2..., proving an actual restart occurred
After restart, apparmor active/enforcing (24 profiles), inventory-app active and enabled, curl to the inventory endpoint succeeded
Captured node2 boot_id 489b0bb4... and confirmed Ansible present prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot acknowledged before disconnect; poll timed out mid-reboot then succeeded with new boot_id 41677490..., proving an actual restart occurred
After restart, Ansible functional on node2 and curl from node2 to node1's inventory app on port 8181 succeeded, confirming cluster connectivity and node1's service health persisted
